extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) practicing before the USPTO; OED/disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing a practitioner’s duties and potential discipline when aware that a Rule 131 declaration (or other prosecution submission) is inaccurate or untrue, and the sanctions/processes that follow such misconduct before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express notice requirement for misrepresentations (Rohm & Haas first requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The first requirement to be met by an applicant, aware of misrepresentation in the prosecution of his application and desiring to overcome it, is that he expressly advise the PTO of its existence, stating specifically wherein it resides." (Rohm and Haas Co. v. Crystal Chemical Co., 722 F.2d 1556, 1572 (Fed. Cir. 1983))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner becomes aware of a misrepresentation in an application or its prosecution, the practitioner must expressly notify the PTO in writing that a misrepresentation exists and identify precisely where it appears in the record. Mere silence or indirect disclosure does not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise actual facts and potential need for further examination (Rohm & Haas second requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The second requirement is that, if the misrepresentation is of one or more facts, the PTO be advised what the actual facts are, the applicant making it clear that further examination in light thereof may be required if any PTO action has been based on the misrepresentation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the misrepresentation concerns factual assertions, the practitioner must set out the true facts and expressly indicate that the PTO may need to reexamine the file in light of the corrected facts. The correction must be in writing and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative obligation to call the examiner's attention to false or misleading Rule 131 declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The practitioner has an affirmative obligation to tell the patent examiner if a Rule 131 declaration is false or misleading."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is insufficient to merely supply accurate facts; the practitioner must specifically call the examiner's attention to the prior untrue or misleading assertions so the examiner knows which statements were false and why the corrected facts matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to fully correct the USPTO written record in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner aware of an inaccuracy or untruth in a filed Rule 131 declaration must advise the Office in writing of the inaccuracy and untruthfulness and fully correct the USPTO written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to notify the Office in writing of known inaccuracies and to correct the record constitutes misconduct. Corrections should be explicit, in writing, and identify both the inaccurate statements and the corrected facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 131 declarations must be truthful (no antedating by false declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rule 131 declaration at issue was prepared to antedate a patent cited as prior art; the declaration must truthfully represent reduction to practice and factual demonstrations asserted to antedate prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must ensure any Rule 131 declaration genuinely supports the factual assertions (e.g., that the inventor reduced the invention to practice on specified dates and demonstrated the claimed features). Preparing or filing a declaration containing untrue assertions to antedate prior art risks inequitable conduct and unenforceability of resulting patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentations can lead to inequitable conduct and patent unenforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: The district court found patents unenforceable due, in part, to a finding that the Rule 131 declaration filed was false; the Federal Circuit affirmed that finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing or permitting false statements in prosecution can be the basis for a court finding of inequitable conduct, which may render affected patents unenforceable. Practitioners should consider the litigation/enforceability risks of false submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) by not advising the Office in writing of the inaccuracy and untruthfulness in the Rule 131 declaration, not advising the Office of the actual facts, and not fully correcting the USPTO written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engaging in conduct that misleads the Office or fails to correct known inaccuracies is proscribed as prejudicial to the administration of justice and can form the basis for disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for this misconduct (suspension, limited recognition, dissociation of credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreed sanction: four-year suspension from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other matters; limited recognition for 30 days to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b); prompt dissociation of Respondent's name from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; prohibition on applying for a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary sanctions may include lengthy suspensions, temporary limited recognition only to comply with administrative obligations, revocation/dissociation of electronic credentials, and restrictions on obtaining new customer numbers until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement timeline and probation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement after 24 months from the Final Order date; must remain suspended until reinstated; upon reinstatement, must serve an eighteen (18) month probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic; it is governed by 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 procedures. If reinstated, practitioners may be subject to probation with monitoring and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause / additional suspension process during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent's address of record, and grant Respondent 15 days to respond; after consideration, the OED Director may request the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional eighteen (18) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The probationary enforcement process includes an opportunity to respond (15 days) but can result in immediate additional suspension if the OED Director persists in the view that probation conditions were violated. Procedures and evidence presented to the USPTO Director will be considered for imposition of further discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED may publish disciplinary records and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a materially consistent notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension and factual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary resolutions are publicized; practitioners should expect publication of the Final Order and a public notice summarizing the misconduct and sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED may consider prior disciplinary records as aggravating factors in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing further complaints or in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent as an aggravating factor, to rebut statements, or in reconsideration requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disciplinary record can be used against a practitioner in future matters — as aggravation or to rebut representations — and may influence sanctions in subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED/USPTO jurisdictional authorities for practitioner discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions against practitioners are taken under statutory and regulatory authority; practitioners should be familiar with these provisions and the Rules of Professional Responsibility / Rules of Professional Conduct applicable at the relevant times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors may influence sanction severity
rubrics_metrics.description: In agreeing to the sanction, the OED Director took into consideration Respondent's declining health and his lack of prior USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal circumstances and prior disciplinary history (or lack thereof) can be considered as mitigating factors in determining the nature and severity of sanctions.
